name: Disaster Artist | Ch2 Starters Revisited
description_md:
Disaster Artist

>In this mini-series I'm focusing on powerful decks built from the Chapter 2 starters. Here Miguel benefits from failure, with [Rabbit's Foot](/card/60560) for card draw, [Old Compass](/card/12083) and [Daniel Jameson](/card/60555) for do-overs, and ["Look what I found!"](/card/12078) for clues. If you're gonna fail, fail in style! `If you want to support my work, give it a like ❤︎ and a favorite ★ on here!`

Series Decks

|   Seeker   |   Survivor   |   Guardian   |    Rogue   |   Mystic   | |:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | Carolyn | Miguel | Tommy| André | Marie |

At a Glance

>| Stats | | >|:---|:---| >| Clue-finding: |  ★★★★☆ | >| Consistency: |  ★★★☆☆ | >| Enemy Management: |  ★★★★☆ | >| Encounter Defense: |  ★★★★★ | >| Survivability: |  ★★★★☆ | >| Simplicity: |  ★★★☆☆ |

Overview

- "Fail" at clue-finding: [Old Compass](/card/12083) allows you to easily find clues on 2 shroud locations with its redo. The shroud lowering effect also allows you to always play ["Look what I found!"](/card/12078) on 3 shroud locations (or 4 during the redo). [Scrape By](/card/12082) and [Stalk Prey](/card/60567) give you further clue-finding options, and all are recurable with [Do-or-Die](/card/60568) and [Hunter's Instinct](/card/60574). [Timely Intervention](/card/12081) then helps you push your luck further while investigating. Any time you fail or play an event, [Rabbit's Foot](/card/60560) and [Knapsack](/card/60552) give card draw (or Knapsack can be used to play events at different locations instead). Don't understimate "Look what I found!" recursion - it's great! - "Fail" at enemy management: With [Daniel Jameson](/card/60555) then any Elusive enemy (including [Feline Hybrid](/card/60553)) is a card draw opportunity. Simply take a basic fight action, likely fail (scaring the enemy away) and so draw a card with [Rabbit's Foot](/card/60560), then repeat the attack. For actions you don't want to fail (e.g. [Guerrilla Tactics](/card/60576) or [Pocketknife](/card/60559) attacks) then Daniel is the perfect safety net. With ["Shove off!"](/card/12079) you can consciously not boost the test, potentially fail, keep "Shove off!" if you do fail, and then use Daniel's redo to fish for its damage. Frequently you can deal 5 damage in a turn (2 with upgraded Guerilla Tactics in your free event action, then 3 Pocket Knife attacks - gaining a resource for a kill). - Succeed at everything else: [Miguel's Knapsack](/card/60552), [Rabbit's Foot](/card/60560) and [Stalk Prey](/card/60567) with [Hunter's Instinct](/card/60574) provide a solid card draw engine. Miguel has robust health and sanity unlike other Ch2 Survivor access investigators, making him sturdy. [Pocketknife](/card/60559), [Emergency Cache](/card/12089) and [Same Old Thing](/card/60561) provide cash or cash-savings - allowing for [Levelheaded](/card/60579) boosts. Obviously this deck doesn't have any cards which utilise Miguel's ability - but I never draw the Elder Sign anyway! Hopefully they'll be more non-trap Tricks in the future that could go in the deck... Thank you: [5argon](https://arkhamdb.com/user/profile/61394/5argon) and [their thumbnail tool](https://arkham-starter.com/tool/thumbnails); [Valentin1331](https://arkhamdb.com/user/profile/42890/Valentin1331) for his support over the years; the community creators of [Arkham.Build](https://www.patreon.com/c/arkhambuild/) ([Felix](https://spoettel.dev/)), [Arkham Cards](https://www.patreon.com/c/arkhamcards/) ([zzorba](https://www.reddit.com/user/zzorba/)) and [ArkhamDB](https://www.patreon.com/c/kamalisk/) ([kamalisk](https://www.reddit.com/user/kamalisk/)) - linking their Patreons!

Starting deck and planned progression

0 XP starting deck is below (and link here): A recommended order of purchases/upgrades is: - [Unexpected Courage](/card/12094) → [Scrape By](/card/12082) - [Old Compass](/card/60558) → [Old Compass ••](/card/12083) - [Hunter's Instinct](/card/12074) → [Hunter's Instinct ••](/card/60574) - [Guerrilla Tactics](/card/60564) → [Guerrilla Tactics ••](/card/60576) - 1 x [Levelheaded](/card/12076) → 1 x [Levelheaded •••](/card/60579) - 1 x [Levelheaded](/card/12076) → 1 x [Respite](/card/60577) Post-19 XP suggestions are: - [Timely Intervention](/card/12081) → [Timely Intervention •••](/card/60582) - A [Makeshift Bomb](/card/60581) if you're keen. ["Shove off!"](/card/12079) is the only thing that can be easily replaced.

Playtesting Notes

On playtesting CoB (Hard, two player, with the 5 bonus XP) I didn't make any changes to the deck other than to lower the consistency rating to 3★. While the card draw does help a bit with consistency, with just 3 cards allowing card draw you can get bad luck and not have any of these - and then the deck grinds to a halt a bit (typically forcing card draw actions to get something to work with). I spent the 5 XP on [upgraded Old Compasses](/card/12083) and one copy of [Scrape By](/card/12082). I think Scenario 1 CoB is bad for this deck, as [Stalk Prey](/card/60567) for clue-finding introduces enemies, and there's enough of those going around already without you actively drawing them! We ended up defeated scenario 1 through damage, with two damage left to go on the boss - but that does give you 3 bonus XP (we secured 7 total). Scenario 2 was a total difference. We tackled it during "day", and using ["Look what I found!"](/card/12078) with [Old Compass](/card/60558) I managed to get all clues off a 4 should Victory location. I also had [Rabbit's Foot](/card/60560) from the first turn, providing enough card draw that I could have cycled. There's a lot of 1 health enemies running around, so [Pocketknife](/card/60559) was helpful to pick these off and earn resources. [Guerrilla Tactics](/card/60576) did some heavy lifting, putting more damage on the boss and allowing for boosted evades. [Hunter's Instinct](/card/60574) was used primarily to recur [Scrape By](/card/12082) and combat events to get extra chip damage on the boss. We finished up with 21 XP total by the end of Scenario 2, and I forwent [upgraded Levelheaded](/card/60579) or [Respite](/card/60577) - instead going for two [upgraded Timely Intervention](/card/60582). Scenario 3 went very well, with a win by turn 6. I got some lucky pulls for Hard difficulty with [Old Compass](/card/60558), used [Scrape By](/card/12082) for [Arcane Lock](/card/12157), and also used [Stalk Prey](/card/60567) for an additional clue. [Upgraded Guerrilla Tactics](/card/60576) put two damage on the boss with a fight action (again a lucky pull - I was expecting to need a [Daniel Jameson](/card/60555) redo and to eat a Retaliate) and then I got a kill-assist in the final turn by committing [upgraded Timely Intervention](/card/60582) to one of my fellow investigator's 4 damage attacks (boosting it to a 14 test - even if they drew all the blood tokens remaining and the -5 it would have been safe. Take that Hard mode!). The fellow investigator is a deck for my next series, so I'll keep it secret for now... As we'd barely begun, I hadn't had time to build up an engine - but the performance was still very good in that classic Survivor vein of getting stuff done regardless of the odds.

Final thoughts

I don't think Chapter 1 ever provided trivial, XP-free recursion of ["Look what I found!"](/card/12078), but it's powerful - especially with [Old Compass](/card/12083). Honestly Miguel is crummy at finding clues otherwise, so being able to get two off a location is great. Compared to [Izzie](/card/12013) or [Daniela](/card/12001), Miguel has beefier combined health and sanity than either of those two - plus his free event action makes the time spent building your asset easier (because you can be playing events for free while you put down assets). Overall I think this is one of the better ways to run fail tech, and it's a change of pace if you don't like traps. While fail tech no longer has flashy payoffs such as [Take Heart](/card/60519), ["Look what I found!"](/card/12078) recursion more than justifies the playstyle. Hope you enjoy!
